subject: Payment routing & invoice samples — procurement readiness check
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Matt Cole <matt.cole@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Payment routing & invoice samples — procurement readiness check

Hi Matt — great to meet on the call this morning. Quick written recap and a few asks so our billing/ops team can accelerate the commercial path.

Recap (from today)
- Use case: clinical decisioning infra + inference at scale for Edge Health pilot.
- Expected steady state: ~2000 reqs/min after Q1 2027 ramp.
- Security/compliance: standard SLA + SOC2 evidence flagged but not blocking procurement.

Procurement / billing items we discussed (asks)
1) Preferred payment method: PO vs card? you mentioned your procurement prefers POs — confirm preferred net terms (Net30/Net45).
2) Billing address and legal name for the vendor record (we need exact line items for invoice).
3) Invoice format: do you require machine-readable invoices (XML/UBL) or is PDF sufficient? If XML, which schema?
4) Tax/VAT specifics: are you subject to any tax exemptions or do we need EIN/TIN on invoices?
5) Marketplace option: are you open to purchasing through AWS/Azure marketplace (simpler procurement) or do you need a direct vendor path?

Next steps from our side
- I can share an example invoice in XML and a W9/EIN stub for your AP team to validate.
- Looping in our billing ops (Kimberly) and sales ops (Ben) to prepare sample files and note any constraints for marketplace purchases.

Could you reply with the billing address and whether a PO (and tentative net terms) is preferred? If XML is required, let us know which schema/version.

Thanks — I’ll follow up internally and send the templates shortly.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189
https://redwood.com
From: Matt Cole <matt.cole@edgehealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lam <sarah.lam@edgehealth.com>, Edge Health Finance Team <finance@edgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Payment routing & invoice samples — procurement readiness check

Thanks, Sergio — good recap. A few answers inline: 

1) Payment method: Our Procurement team requires a PO for any vendor invoicing > $10k/month. Net terms: we standardly do Net30 but can discuss Net45 with finance if needed.
2) Billing/legal name and address: Edge Health, Inc.
   Attn: Accounts Payable
   1209 Market St, Suite 400
   San Francisco, CA 94103
   EIN: 94-1234567

3) Invoice format: AP prefers PDF, but our ERP can ingest XML UBL 2.1. If you can provide both a PDF and an XML UBL 2.1 sample, that would be ideal.
4) Tax: No VAT — domestic US vendor; include EIN on invoices.
5) Marketplace: Procurement is open to marketplace purchases if pricing and terms map to the contract — however, they prefer a direct vendor record for the pilot to simplify PO control.

If you can send an XML sample and a brief note on how the marketplace flow differs (timing, invoicing cadence, billing contact), that will help.

Matt
Matt Cole
Director, Procurement Operations
Edge Health
matt.cole@edgehealth.com | +1 (415) 622-3344

Also flag any legal or tax caveats for our contracts team if the customer requests marketplace procurement later.

Thanks — want to get these to Matt by EOD today so they can validate with their ERP team.

Sergio — attaching the sample files. Notes:
- invoice_example.xml: UBL 2.1 structure, minimal line items, includes vendor EIN.
- W9_EdgeHealth_stub.pdf: W9 stub (redacted) for AP to verify EIN format.
- net_terms_options.csv: rows = Net15, Net30, Net45 + impact on collections cadence and invoice aging.

Marketplace note: we can list Redwood on AWS Marketplace but the onboarding takes ~2-3 weeks and requires our pricing to be public for that listing; if Edge Health wants private pricing, direct vendor is faster. For PO-based workflows, the marketplace will still generate invoices that the buyer's ERP ingests, but there is a reconciliation step on both sides.

Attaching: invoice_example.xml; W9_EdgeHealth_stub.pdf; net_terms_options.csv
